children: Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE:LLY) raised guidance as Mounjaro, Zepbound and Foundayo deliver heart‑benefit and obesity data—from FDA label expansion and SURPASS‑CVOT to real‑world Zepbound cost reductions—while strategic moves include Merida acquisition and a federal drug‑pricing agreement.
: Eli Lilly (LLY): FDA expanded Mounjaro label to include reduced major adverse cardiovascular events in at‑risk type 2 diabetes patients, supported by SURPASS‑CVOT long‑term trial results.
: Eli Lilly raised full-year revenue outlook to $85–$87B. Mounjaro and Zepbound drive a large share of sales. Prescription fulfillment and pipeline progress cited as key to hitting guidance.
: Eli Lilly (LLY) reported Foundayo, its oral obesity pill, showed non‑inferior reduction in major cardiovascular events versus a long‑acting insulin in type 2 diabetes patients with obesity.
: Eli Lilly (LLY) joined a Trump-era drug-pricing deal, cutting prices for federal programs and joining tariff relief in exchange for aligning U.S. prices closer to international levels.
: Eli Lilly (LLY) real-world claims on 15,843 adults 55+ starting Zepbound show lower hospital and ER use and 6‑ and 12‑month medical cost reductions (excludes drug costs).
: Eli Lilly (LLY) to acquire Merida Biosciences for up to $2.88B in cash, adding Merida’s immunity and allergy programs to Lilly’s development pipeline.
: Eli Lilly (LLY): Phase 3b TOGETHER-PsO and TOGETHER-PsA show adding tirzepatide to ixekizumab maintained or improved skin, joint and metabolic outcomes through Week 52 versus ixekizumab alone.
